# Production-Specific Contract Discovery

Work-wide and cross-layer outcomes that every authored H2 population revisits. Layer-local requirements belong in that layer's discovery file, and conditions shared only by treatments, scripts, and screenplays belong in `films.md`.

## Shared and local boundary {#shared-local-boundary}

Determine which recurring production-wide or cross-layer conditions remain unowned after applying the shared principles and obligations. Search the production's directives, identity, promise, subject, sources, assets, dependencies, risks, and observed failures without treating those inputs as a checklist. An independent result has its own applicability, intended effect, and observable failure boundary; a concrete answer to an existing shared question is not a new rule.

A positive acknowledgement identifies each retained result. If none exists, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete inputs and risks examined and the shared owners that fully cover them. A label, aspiration, copied item, or audit assertion is not a result.

Review question: which production-specific condition remains independently applicable after the shared graph answers its complete reusable questions?

Sources: [NASA on eliciting and validating requirements from stakeholder needs and system context](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/4-1-stakeholder-expectations-definition/); [ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 on requirements quality](https://www.iso.org/standard/72089.html)

## Canonical realization {#canonical-realization}

Give every retained result one semantic owner, an observable stage-appropriate realization, and any additive claim its independent evidence behavior requires. Do not leave an adopted rule only in `.wiki`, a planning note, an issue, or prose instructions, and do not create an empty target.

A positive acknowledgement identifies the current owner and stage-appropriate realization, plus any independent target and claim the result requires. An exclusion is valid only when the boundary search found no independent result, not when implementation is deferred.

Review question: where is each retained result owned, realized, and wired so a later layer cannot silently replace or omit it?

Sources: [NASA on requirements verification matrices](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/); [W3C PROV-O on responsibility and derivation](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/)

# Settings Discovery

The settings-specific outcomes that the complete settings H2 population must search for and account for. Apply `common.md` in the same pass for broader production contracts.

## Directive, promise, and subject requirements {#directive-promise-subject-requirements}

Discover production-specific facts, constraints, entities, dependencies, uncertainties, and boundaries required by direct directives, the delivery promise and form, existing canon and assets, subject or medium knowledge, source conflicts, and representation risks. Give each result an H2 owner or a truthful inherited-default, outside-scope, or unresolved classification. Search openly; do not fill a predetermined domain list.

A positive acknowledgement names the current owners or classifications. If none lies beyond shared coverage, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete inputs and risks examined and the shared owners that suffice. A future owner, empty file family, or audit assertion is not a result.

Review question: which direct input, promised observation, operative subject, dependency, or failure risk still lacks a settings owner or explicit classification?

Sources: [Ryan on storyworlds as reconstructed systems rather than closed inventories](https://marilaur.info/degrees.pdf); [NASA on eliciting requirements from actual stakeholder and system context](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/4-1-stakeholder-expectations-definition/)

## Planned delivery backcast {#planned-delivery-backcast}

Backcast the production's actual planned consumers to discover every production-wide fact or constraint they would otherwise have to invent. For a film, inspect planned treatments, scripts, screenplays, design branches, shots, production source, and edit. For a brief, inspect the bounded observations, design branches, shots, production source, and edit. For a library, inspect the selected design and source branches and any production serialization. Put consequential canon in settings before downstream use; route narrative order, design decisions, shot realization, and edit choices to their own owners.

A positive acknowledgement identifies the settings owners and any separately activated production contract. If the planned consumers need no additional owner, one population-wide exclusion names the consumers examined and the existing owners that make invention unnecessary.

Review question: which planned downstream consumer would still have to invent a production-wide fact, permission, constraint, identity, or review condition?

Sources: [Plan-and-Write on separating planning from realization](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33017378); [NASA systems engineering handbook on allocation and bidirectional traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

# Brief Discovery

The brief-specific outcome that the complete active brief H2 population must search for and account for. Apply `common.md` in the same pass for broader contracts.

## Work-specific brief requirements {#work-specific-brief-requirements}

Discover every production-specific delivery, shot-allocation, viewing-condition, observation, acceptance, representation, sound, silence, or transition condition needed to answer the bounded brief without importing an unnecessary film ladder. Derive the requirements from the actual promised result rather than a generic turntable, demonstration, or short-form recipe, and give each material result an actual brief H2 owner or a production-local principle, obligation, or evidence relationship with a typed claim.

A positive acknowledgement identifies the current authored owners and contract wiring. If the complete search finds no independent brief result, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete delivery, observation, falsifiability, and realization risks examined and the shared owners that fully cover them. A format label, shot count, style aspiration, or assertion that the result is simple does not cover this duty.

Review question: which bounded delivery or observation condition is specific to this production and absent from the reusable brief contract?

Sources: [NIST definition of verification as objective evidence against specified requirements](https://www.nist.gov/glossary-term/34441); [NASA systems engineering handbook on defining verification objectives](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

# Design Discovery

The outcome for production-specific conditions shared by the active map, model, space, material, instance, motion, and system branches. Every active design branch applies this file with `common.md` and its own branch discovery file. Production-wide conditions belong in `common.md`, and conditions unique to one branch belong in that branch's file.

## Work-specific design requirements {#work-specific-design-requirements}

Discover every production-specific condition that must remain compatible across the active design branches. Representation ceilings, precision and tolerance conventions, falsifying observations, interface and assembly rules, reuse boundaries, identifier conventions, and degradation behavior are possible search directions rather than a checklist. Derive the requirements from the actual settings, directives, source assets, dependencies, planned consumers, and delivery or library promise rather than a generic asset pipeline. Give each independent result one earliest design H2 owner or a production-local principle, obligation, or evidence relationship with a typed claim over every affected population.

A positive acknowledgement identifies the production target, current semantic owner, affected branch wiring, and stage-appropriate realization. If the complete search finds no independent cross-branch design result, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete representation, measurement, interface, reuse, identity, observation, and degradation risks examined and the shared owners that fully cover them. A fidelity label, tolerance value without an applicability boundary, file-format convention, or assertion that the branches are compatible does not cover this duty.

Review question: which production-specific design condition must be shared across active branches so their independently authored results remain compatible and falsifiable?

Sources: [NASA systems engineering handbook appendix on interface responsibilities, coordinate systems, units, and tolerances](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/); [NIST on metrology, traceability, test methods, and measurement uncertainty](https://www.nist.gov/metrology)

# Instance Discovery

The instance-specific outcome that the complete active instance H2 population must search for and account for. Apply `common.md` and `designs.md` in the same pass for broader production contracts.

## Work-specific instance requirements {#work-specific-instance-requirements}

Discover every production-specific population condition required by the actual repeated subjects and their placement context. Membership and stable identity, prototype selection, controlled variation, transform and grounding, density or spacing, overlap, ordering, level-of-detail tiers, seed behavior, and representative observations are possible search directions rather than a checklist. Derive the requirements from the governed population, reviewed prototypes, governing maps or containing spaces, material variation, planned motion, and promised use rather than a generic scatter or grid recipe, and give each material result an actual instance H2 owner or a production-local principle, obligation, or evidence relationship with a typed claim.

A positive acknowledgement identifies the current authored owners and contract wiring. If the complete search finds no independent instance result, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete membership, identity, variation, grounding, density, overlap, ordering, tier, seed, and observation risks examined and the shared owners that fully cover them. A count, seed, distribution name, or density label without its applicability, derivation, and falsifying population observation does not cover this duty.

Review question: which repeated-population condition is specific to these members and their placement context and absent from the reusable instance contract?

Sources: [OpenUSD PointInstancer on prototypes, ids, transforms, masks, velocities, and extents](https://openusd.org/dev/api/class_usd_geom_point_instancer.html); [glTF `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing` on per-instance transforms and accessors](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/main/extensions/2.0/Vendor/EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing)

## Work-specific instance requirements {#work-specific-instance-requirements}

Discover every production-specific population condition required by the actual repeated subjects and their placement context. Membership and stable identity, prototype selection, controlled variation, transform and grounding, density or spacing, overlap, ordering, level-of-detail tiers, seed behavior, and representative observations are possible search directions rather than a checklist. Derive the requirements from the governed population, reviewed prototypes, governing maps or containing spaces, material variation, planned motion, and promised use rather than a generic scatter or grid recipe, and give each material result an actual instance H2 owner or a production-local principle, obligation, or evidence relationship with a typed claim.

A positive acknowledgement identifies the current authored owners and contract wiring. If the complete search finds no independent instance result, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete membership, identity, variation, grounding, density, overlap, ordering, tier, seed, and observation risks examined and the shared owners that fully cover them. A count, seed, distribution name, or density label without its applicability, derivation, and falsifying population observation does not cover this duty.

Review question: which repeated-population condition is specific to these members and their placement context and absent from the reusable instance contract?

Sources: [OpenUSD PointInstancer on prototypes, ids, transforms, masks, velocities, and extents](https://openusd.org/dev/api/class_usd_geom_point_instancer.html); [glTF `EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing` on per-instance transforms and accessors](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/tree/main/extensions/2.0/Vendor/EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing)

# Material Discovery

The material-specific outcome that the complete active material H2 population must search for and account for. Apply `common.md` and `designs.md` in the same pass for broader production contracts.

## Work-specific material requirements {#work-specific-material-requirements}

Discover every production-specific construction, finish, appearance, or state condition required by the actual surface system and its planned observations. Physical scale, projection and orientation, layer or channel relation, host binding, junction behavior, optical response, authored state, variation, weathering, and fallback are possible search directions rather than a checklist. Derive the requirements from the governed materials, source assets, bound model or space surfaces, lighting and delivery conditions, and promised use rather than a generic physically based shading preset, and give each material result an actual material H2 owner or a production-local principle, obligation, or evidence relationship with a typed claim.

A positive acknowledgement identifies the current authored owners and contract wiring. If the complete search finds no independent material result, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete scale, projection, binding, junction, response, state, variation, asset, and observation risks examined and the shared owners that fully cover them. A material name, texture set, color value, or style label without its surface applicability and observable response does not cover this duty.

Review question: which finish-system condition is specific to these surfaces and absent from the reusable material contract?

Sources: [MaterialX specification on interoperable material, shading, and geometry relationships](https://materialx.org/Specification.html); [glTF 2.0 on materials, textures, texture coordinate sets, and texture transforms](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#materials)

# Film Discovery

The outcomes for production-specific conditions shared by treatments, scripts, and screenplays. Settings anticipates them during backcast, and each of those three authored layers rechecks them. Work-wide conditions belong in `common.md`, and conditions unique to treatments, scripts, or screenplays belong in that layer's discovery file.

## Work-specific film requirements {#work-specific-film-requirements}

Discover every production-specific condition that must survive across treatment design, executable staging, and final audiovisual expression. Form, progression, audience access, visual or textual language, representation, sound, silence, and recurring devices are possible search directions rather than a checklist. Put each independent result in the production target matching its evidence behavior and configure stage-aligned claims over treatments, scripts, and screenplays. During settings backcast, establish the contract and its settings prerequisites without inventing film content; each layer realizes it in current authored owners.

A retained contract records its production target, three-layer claim wiring, settings prerequisites, and current authored realization in each layer. If the complete search finds no independent cross-layer film result, one population-wide exclusion names the concrete formal, access, representation, and audiovisual risks examined and the shared owners that fully cover them. A genre name, style label, formal aspiration, or rule active on only one intended layer does not cover this duty.

Review question: which production-specific condition must remain recognizable and testable across treatments, scripts, and screenplays?

Sources: [Jakobson on the dominant organizing other elements of a work](https://archive.org/details/readingsinrussia0000mate); [Bordwell on films as patterned systems that guide spectator construction](https://www.routledge.com/Narration-in-the-Fiction-Film/Bordwell/p/book/9780415018777); [Chion on sound and image forming one audiovisual mode of perception](https://cup.columbia.edu/book/audio-vision-sound-on-screen/9780231185882/)

# 한국어 의무

## 번역 간섭과 레지스터 모집단 장부 {#korean-population-interference-account}

```contract-rule
{
  "id": "korean-population-interference-account",
  "status": "active",
  "safeApplication": "population-distribution",
  "timing": "after the complete selected Korean-language population exists",
  "sourceIdentity": "campaign-2363-b25-language@8b03cf3b80d205f71d2ba1f5c52c90a02c050b5b"
}
```

한 계층이 완성되면 선언한 한국어 변이를 유창하게 읽는 심사자가 증거 주석을 제외한 전 모집단을 먼저 읽는다. 장면, 화자, 압력과 종결이 다른데도 직역 절 조립, 주어 과잉, 명사화, 높임 또는 설명 골격이 기능 없이 수렴하는지 실제 문장별로 비교하고 후렴, 제도 문서와 인물 말버릇처럼 소유된 반복은 보존한다.

검토 질문: 서로 다른 소재에서 기능 없이 지배하는 한국어 골격은 무엇이며 어떤 실제 구성원이 그 판정을 입증하는가?

출처: [Padmakumar와 He의 모델 보조 글쓰기 다양성 연구](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05196); [국립국어원 한국어기초사전](https://krdict.korean.go.kr/)

## 독자 언어 접근 {#korean-audience-language-access}

```contract-rule
{
  "id": "korean-audience-language-access",
  "status": "active",
  "safeApplication": "population-distribution",
  "timing": "after the complete selected Korean-language population exists",
  "sourceIdentity": "campaign-2363-b25-language@8b03cf3b80d205f71d2ba1f5c52c90a02c050b5b"
}
```

전체 모집단은 설명되지 않은 언어 전환, 전문어, 시대어, 자막, 인용과 번역 판본의 의미와 출처와 상태를 의도 독자가 식별하게 하되 작품이 보존하기로 한 차이를 지우지 않는다.

검토 질문: 어느 한국어 경계 때문에 의도 독자가 제작 결정을 이해하거나 그 출처와 상태를 구분할 수 없는가?

출처: [W3C 언어 협상 안내](https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-lang-priorities); [W3C TTML2](https://www.w3.org/TR/ttml2/)

# Common obligations

Duties each selected authored-layer population satisfies in that layer's own terms. An item no unit cites is missing coverage; several units cite an item wherever its wording calls for several owners. No obligation is a checklist, and none permits exclusion.

## Purpose fit {#purpose-fit}

Each authored file performs one or more roles needed by the production promise and the scope of the current delivery. Connect material that does not contribute to those roles with another element or remove it.

Judge this by what the file population actually includes and omits. The author must be able to explain how those choices serve the production promise.

Review question: which file roles does this population need, and what later decision or delivered observation would become underdetermined if each role disappeared?

This item asks why a file as a whole is needed. Specialist addressability obligations govern independent ownership by authored units, the common scope-preservation principle governs each unit's required scope, and narrative unit function governs the need for an individual narrative unit.

Sources: [Jakobson on the dominant that orders the functions of other elements](https://archive.org/details/readingsinrussia0000mate); [Burton and Poster on the distinct work done by beginnings, endings, tension, and pace](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/book-you-need-to-read-to-write-the-book-you-want-to-write/beginnings-and-endings-tension-and-pace/7B84CB546C696FD1B6A8AB753522B42C)

## Layer boundary {#layer-boundary}

Each authored file declares one document role and contains only decisions recognized by that role's specialist principle or obligation family. A mixed-role file is split, and a missing decision begins in the layer whose contracts own it before being carried downward. This common obligation owns routing and single-role composition; the specialist contracts define the content of each role.

Review question: which decision in each file requires a second specialist family to justify it, and where must that decision move?

This item asks which layer owns a decision. The common substantive-completion principle asks whether each addressed unit is complete at that layer.

Sources: [Plan-and-Write on separating planning from realization](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33017378); [Detailed Outline Control on controlling generation through an explicit intermediate plan](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10077)

## Production language {#production-language}

The authored population uses the primary working language declared in settings with enough grammatical and terminological consistency for its intended readers. Exact identifiers, source titles, quotations, established technical terms, and deliberately authored multilingual content may retain another language when their function and audience access remain explicit.

Review question: can the intended reader understand every production decision across the population without guessing across inconsistent language, unexplained terminology, or an unowned language switch?

This item owns the linguistic accessibility of the authored population. Settings owns which working and audience-facing languages the production selected, while screenplay and film source own the content and timing of dialogue, captions, and audible language.

Sources: [W3C Internationalization on declaring language in HTML](https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-html-language-declarations); [BBC screenplay format and language presentation](https://downloads.bbc.co.uk/writersroom/scripts/screenplay.pdf); [W3C Timed Text Markup Language](https://www.w3.org/TR/ttml2/)

## Proportionate development {#proportionate-development}

Across the complete selected population, unit count and granularity, authored body within each unit, and internal progression are proportionate to the declared production scale and to the importance of represented subjects, transitions, narrative turns, observations, and implementation decisions. Major work is not compressed into a few umbrella units or short reports, and minor work is not inflated to imitate completeness. Compare siblings and assign greater concrete development and consequence to the material whose production effect is greater.

For the narrative ladder, record every complete layer body excluding comments. Treatments establish the flat event baseline. Compare the script population with that baseline in whole and use their many-to-many evidence edges to read the units that realize each treatment event. Scripts and screenplays share the delivery partition, so compare each group and unit as well as both populations in whole. A downstream narrative layer whose authored body does not exceed its parent's has restated that parent or dropped work its layer owes. When the production's chosen form genuinely requires the opposite, settings states the reason instead of leaving the comparison unmade. Settings inherits no authored layer and answers from its own population.

A brief performs the same audit inside its delivery, shot, and observation hierarchy: record the H2/H3/H4 population and authored-body distribution, then read whether each depth adds the bounded staging or falsifying observation its parent leaves to it. Do not demand that one concise observation be longer than the shot it tests; the comparison detects a collapsed hierarchy, while the literal question decides whether the observation is sufficient.

Do not compare prose length across design -> source. Source is TypeScript, so character count against a design document proves nothing. At that boundary, compare whether every selected design H2 is realized and whether consequential design decisions receive proportionate implementation depth. Library asset count, spatial level or zone count, representation variation, source-owner distribution, and required neutral observations are scale signals in their own terms.

When the user specifies runtime, delivery-group or episode count, shot budget, asset count, building extent, life span, historical interval, or another production scale, that scale governs every layer in the form the layer can answer. A layer carrying a delivery partition answers with that partition and its allocation. A layer without one answers whether its material can sustain the declared scale and whether it would overrun it. That is the earliest place either failure is visible and the last place it is cheap to repair.

When rewriting the same scope, the earlier version's group directories, unit files, selected H2/H3/H4 counts, authored body excluding comments, distribution by unit, asset and source-owner counts, required observation population, and research breadth are regression alarms. Counts do not prove quality, but a result in which several measures collapse together without an approved scope change is not complete.

Structure and amount detect a regression; literal reading judges whether the material is actually sufficient. A longer layer can merely expand a parent's wording. The narrative parent-differentiation principle and each layer's authoring gate decide whether the added body contains decisions owned by that layer.

This obligation asks only about quantity and allocation across the population. The scope-preservation principle asks whether required content exists, the substantive-completion principle asks whether each addressed unit is a real layer deliverable, and specialist addressability obligations ask whether the population chose truthful unit boundaries.

Review question: what do the recorded sibling, parent-layer, declared-scale, and earlier-version comparisons expose as compressed below its consequence or expanded without production work, and what does a literal read of the complete population decide?

When this obligation fails, redesign the complete selected population and its unit boundaries, expand consequential units, and split overloaded owners before advancing the layer. Stop downstream authorship until the earliest disproportionate layer is repaired. Do not thin units into summaries merely to retain an unworkable count.

Sources: [CONCOCT on underdeveloped major events and overdeveloped minor events in long-form generation](https://aclanthology.org/2023.findings-emnlp.723/); [Hicks on scale as an organizing relation of time, distance, and narrative progress](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/scale-crisis-and-the-modern-novel/introduction/2DC3BA9BA9CF6C3DE80AD1A2A52FFDCB); [NASA systems engineering handbook on allocation and verification](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

# Common obligations

Duties each selected authored-layer population satisfies in that layer's own terms. An item no unit cites is missing coverage; several units cite an item wherever its wording calls for several owners. No obligation is a checklist, and none permits exclusion.

## Purpose fit {#purpose-fit}

Each authored file performs one or more roles needed by the production promise and the scope of the current delivery. Connect material that does not contribute to those roles with another element or remove it.

Judge this by what the file population actually includes and omits. The author must be able to explain how those choices serve the production promise.

Review question: which file roles does this population need, and what later decision or delivered observation would become underdetermined if each role disappeared?

This item asks why a file as a whole is needed. Specialist addressability obligations govern independent ownership by authored units, the common scope-preservation principle governs each unit's required scope, and narrative unit function governs the need for an individual narrative unit.

## Layer boundary {#layer-boundary}

Each authored file declares one document role and contains only decisions recognized by that role's specialist principle or obligation family. # Post-draft anti-default obligations

These questions become meaningful only after one selected authored population is complete. Counts locate literal passages and never decide merit, provenance, or authorship.

## Recurrent frame distribution {#recurrent-frame-distribution}

```contract-rule
{
  "id": "sh-recurrent-frame-distribution",
  "status": "active",
  "safeApplication": "post-draft-frequency",
  "timing": "after the complete selected authored population exists",
  "sourceIdentity": "campaign-2363-b25@8b03cf3b80d205f71d2ba1f5c52c90a02c050b5b"
}
```

Group repeated contrasts, qualifications, enumerations, transitions, predicates, and closures by their literal operation. Different material may share a frame when refrain, ritual, institutional form, accessibility convention, or another declared constraint owns it; recurrence with no shared material function is repaired at the smallest responsible owners.

Review question: which frame recurs across unlike material, which complete membership establishes the pattern, and what production-owned function protects any retained use?

Sources: [Padmakumar and He on measured diversity loss in model-assisted writing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05196)

## Surface cadence distribution {#surface-cadence-distribution}

```contract-rule
{
  "id": "sh-surface-cadence-distribution",
  "status": "active",
  "safeApplication": "population-distribution",
  "timing": "after the complete selected authored population exists",
  "sourceIdentity": "campaign-2363-b25@8b03cf3b80d205f71d2ba1f5c52c90a02c050b5b"
}
```

Map sentence length, paragraph movement, breaks, emphasis, and handoff patterns to the pressures and forms they carry. Deliberately even procedure and formal repetition pass; unrelated operations converging on one cadence without cause do not. Repair the material boundary rather than injecting random variation.

Review question: which cadence dominates materially different units, and does the production own the reason for that regularity?

Sources: [Padmakumar and He on measured diversity loss in model-assisted writing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05196); [Purdue OWL on repeated sentence patterns](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/general_writing/academic_writing/sentence_variety/similar_sentence_patterns_or_rhythms.html)

# Settings obligations

These required roles must be covered across the settings H2 population. They permit no exclusion: every production shape has an addressable canon, delivery boundary, governing aim, production-wide visual and fidelity contract, build-or-adopt scope, audience or operator access contract, accessibility-deliverable classification, coordinate and unit convention, reproducible delivery review condition, coverage map, accounting for independently consequential subjects and any conditions the design serves, explicit inherited-default boundary, and coherent production system.

## Addressable canon {#addressable-canon}

The settings population gives every independently citable, revisable, falsifiable, or reviewable production fact or constraint one stable canonical H2. Subjects, relationships, places, events outside the delivered action, resources, rules, capabilities, limits, delivery facts, and uncertainty with different consumers or change paths are not hidden in overview prose, subordinate headings, tables, or another owner's description.

A file is a domain namespace rather than an evidence address. An H2 contains only attributes inseparable from its one owner and points to facts owned elsewhere instead of redefining them.

Review question: which statement could change or be cited independently and therefore still lacks its own settings H2 owner?

This obligation owns the settings address structure. The common scope-preservation principle owns missing required scope, and the common substantive-completion principle owns the depth of each existing H2.

Sources: [NASA on unique identification and one requirement per statement](https://swehb.nasa.gov/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=146540037); [Marie-Laure Ryan on storyworld entities and states](https://marilaur.info/degrees.pdf); [ttsc on host and reference unit coverage](https://ttsc.dev/docs/evidence/claims/)

## Delivery scope {#delivery-scope}

The settings define the exact deliverable boundary, including whether this package is a film, a direct brief, or a reusable design library, what it contains, and where it ends.

Review question: what is the last reviewable artifact this production promises to deliver?

Sources: [NASA systems engineering handbook on stakeholder expectations and system boundaries](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

## Governing aim {#governing-aim}

The settings define the single production promise against which all lower-layer choices are judged, including the audience or operator and the observation that matters most.

Review question: which one sentence resolves a tradeoff between two otherwise valid implementation choices?

Sources: [Jakobson on the dominant that orders the functions of other elements](https://archive.org/details/readingsinrussia0000mate)

## Production visual grammar {#production-visual-grammar}

The settings population defines the production-wide color, silhouette, proportion, scale, material language, state vocabulary, and intentional exceptions needed to make the delivered parts one visual world. It reconciles conflicting references and assigns the scope of every shared rule or approved departure without replacing the subject-specific geometry, surface, or spatial decisions owned by design branches. When an external derived rendition becomes an audience surface, this owner constrains its shared positive and negative prompt language, continuity, and exception boundaries. Each applicable design H2 owns the exact per-shot prompt, negative prompt, seed, strength, scalar controls, and registered references within those boundaries, while `production-fidelity-tier` owns the generator adoption and preservation ceiling. Every request cites or mechanically encodes those settings and design owners instead of becoming an unreviewed second design authority.

Review question: which delivered subject, place, state, or rendition still requires an implementer to invent or privately override the visual language that joins it to the rest of the production?

This obligation owns the authored visual system and its scope. `governing-aim` owns the audience or operator effect that system serves, while `obligations/delivery/production-sources.md#shared-visual-grammar` owns faithful engine-facing serialization of already authored shared values.

Sources: [OpenUSD on composition and asset structure](https://openusd.org/release/glossary.html); [glTF 2.0 on scenes, nodes, meshes, and materials](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#concepts); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

## Production fidelity tier {#production-fidelity-tier}

The settings population defines each promised delivery's representation tier, target observation conditions, and the visible inferences that tier is and is not authorized to support. It states whether deterministic structure is itself the audience delivery or the technical truth beneath an external derived rendition, and which structure, identity, continuity, preservation-strength boundary, and acceptance claims the rendition must preserve. When it selects a derived rendition, it also selects the exact provider, model, immutable version, execution boundary, accepted cost basis, and reasoned production consumer under current research; research retains source, license or terms, review-date, capability, and availability facts. Preview, diagnostic, blocking, deterministic, derived, and publication outputs remain distinguishable by reviewed purpose and evidence rather than filename, raster, or aspiration alone.

Review question: what observation may the intended recipient legitimately make from each promised output, and which stronger inference must the production explicitly refuse?

This obligation owns production-wide delivery fidelity. `delivery-review-condition` owns the reproducible frame, distance, camera, control, or sample under which that promise is judged, `obligations/design/models.md#representation-ceiling` owns the shared ceiling of the selected model population, and each design H2 owns the particular representation it authorizes within those boundaries.

Sources: [OpenUSD on model kinds and asset resolution](https://openusd.org/release/glossary.html); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master); [NASA systems engineering handbook on verification against intended use](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

## Subject breakdown and production scope {#subject-breakdown-production-scope}

The settings population derives the complete set of subjects, places, states, variants, external references, and cross-branch dependencies the promised delivery requires, then assigns each item to build, adopt, reuse, derive, defer, or explicit outside-scope disposition. Every retained item states the responsible design or source branch, budget or feasibility constraint, authority, and acceptance consequence needed to prevent a placeholder, incidental reference, or unpriced assumption from becoming the delivered asset plan. # Direct brief obligations

Duties the complete brief H2 owner population satisfies across its bounded delivery, shot, and observation hierarchy. An item appears once or more, as its wording requires, across those owners; H3 and H4 descendants provide the owned detail rather than repeating the obligation population. They permit no exclusion.

## Single-scope eligibility {#single-scope-eligibility}

The complete brief population states one observable production question that can be completely answered without a multi-scene causal, choice, or disclosure structure. If downstream work would have to invent such a structure, the production is a film regardless of runtime.

Review question: can the requested result be stated as one bounded falsifiable question, or does it require independent deliveries or a causal ladder?

This obligation decides whether the requested result qualifies for the brief shape. The no-narrative-smuggling principle separately checks every authored unit after selection against that boundary.

Sources: [NIST definition of verification as objective evidence against specified requirements](https://www.nist.gov/glossary-term/34441); [NASA systems engineering handbook on defining verification objectives](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

## Brief unit addressability {#brief-unit-addressability}

The complete brief population gives every independently changeable, citable, or reviewable delivery, shot, and observation its own H2, H3, or H4 address. An H3 does not hide a second shot with its own composition, viewing condition, or acceptance boundary in direct prose, and an H4 does not combine observations that use different conditions or falsify different claims. Split hidden independent work and merge fragments that cannot move, change, or be judged independently.

A change of camera, time, subject, pass, or viewing condition is evidence of a possible boundary rather than an automatic split. H2 and H3 units organize their actual descendants instead of substituting direct prose for the address that an independently useful descendant requires.

Review question: does the brief population hide any independently changeable delivery, shot, or observation, or does any split separate material that cannot move, change, be cited, or be judged independently?

This obligation owns the semantic boundaries of the brief population. Single-scope eligibility decides whether an independent delivery means the production is not a brief; addressability refuses to hide that delivery merely to preserve the selected shape. Observable progression owns whether the requested observation contract is completely allocated across the resulting population, and the brief information-structure principle owns the arrangement inside each resulting unit.

## Observable progression {#observable-progression}

The complete brief population allocates its observable contract: the H2 delivery states the bounded question and overall initial-to-terminal progression, each H3 shot assigns the portion it presents, and each H4 observation states the viewing condition and result that can answer or falsify that portion. # Film source obligations

These obligations divide assembly of reviewed local shots into the global audience timeline across the selected film-source population. Film source owns editorial mapping and auxiliary tracks, while screenplay or brief owns their meaning and shot source owns each local visual realization.

## Editorial-only assembly {#editorial-only-assembly}

Every video edit selects an authored shot, source interval, global start, handle, and transition without inventing local action, a subject capability, or a camera decision. Overlap is explicit, and the assembled endpoint equals the production runtime.

Review question: can every global video interval be traced to one reviewed local shot and every overlap to a declared transition?

Sources: [SMPTE standards overview for time and synchronization](https://www.smpte.org/standards); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

## Authored auxiliary tracks {#authored-auxiliary-tracks}

Every caption, audible item, timeline effect track, and intentionally silent structural track is authorized upstream with exact audience content and timing where those are creative choices. Every required accessibility product from `obligations/core/settings.md#accessibility-deliverable-states` that belongs to a film timeline or language version has an explicit track mapping; an intentionally absent or unsupported product is never disguised as an empty successful track. Shot-local visual effects remain owned by shot source. Pipeline fixtures remain visibly inert and are named as fixtures.

Review question: where are the text, language, audible meaning, effect, and time of every required non-video track authored and mapped, and would deleting a fixture leave audience meaning unchanged?

Sources: [W3C Timed Text Markup Language](https://www.w3.org/TR/ttml2/); [Web Audio API](https://www.w3.org/TR/webaudio/); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

## Deterministic timeline {#deterministic-timeline}

The edit is a pure build from the opened production context and fixed authored values. It carries no hidden clock, mutable history, asset discovery, or conditional creative fallback.

Review question: does the same reviewed source and context always produce the same ordered tracks and exact runtime?

Sources: [ECMAScript language specification](https://tc39.es/ecma262/); [Web Animations timing model](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#timing-model)

# Production source obligations

These obligations divide serialization of production-wide settings across the selected production-source population. Source is neither a second settings document nor a place to author subject construction, motion, scene action, or editorial timing.

## Settings-only serialization {#settings-only-serialization}

Every production-source value implements an authored settings decision or derives mechanically from one. A source value that changes the intended subject, action, story, or edit belongs upstream or in its own downstream source layer instead.

Review question: which exact settings unit owns each creative value, and is every remaining transformation purely mechanical?

Sources: [NASA systems engineering handbook on allocation and bidirectional traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

## Delivery identity {#delivery-identity}

Production identity, logline, target runtime, frame format, delivery mode, and required deliverables remain mutually consistent and match the authored delivery contract. Template or integration fixtures are identified as such and may not masquerade as audience content. Palette, silhouette, and scale consistency belong exclusively to the shared-visual-grammar rule.

Review question: could the engine recover the complete non-visual delivery envelope without guessing, and does no emitted field promise an unauthored result?

Sources: [NASA systems engineering handbook on system boundaries and verification](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

## Shared visual grammar {#shared-visual-grammar}

Every production-wide color, silhouette, scale, material-language, state-vocabulary, and fidelity value implements `obligations/core/settings.md#production-visual-grammar` or `#production-fidelity-tier` without adding an independent aesthetic choice. Subject-specific geometry and materials remain in their specialist source populations, while viewer surfaces consume the same production background rather than maintaining an independent look.

Review question: which shared visual or fidelity value lacks one authored settings owner, is redefined by a source consumer, or is not reused everywhere it governs?

Sources: [glTF 2.0 scene, material, and asset concepts](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#concepts); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

# Shot source obligations

These obligations divide responsibility across TypeScript shot deliveries and their adjacent acceptance exports. Delivery exports own local composition and deterministic shot time; acceptance exports own falsifying observations. Final timeline assembly and auxiliary tracks belong to film source. The separate exact scene edge keeps every governed export tied to one screenplay scene or brief shot.

## Contract-only composition {#contract-only-composition}

Every shot delivery export composes the local visual portion of exactly one screenplay scene or brief shot and introduces no new story event, subject capability, model construction decision, motion path, caption, sound, or editorial transition. It owns composition, camera, lighting, and the orchestration needed to realize that portion of its parent.

Review question: which line would change the delivered meaning if removed, and where is that meaning authorized upstream?

Sources: [NASA systems engineering handbook on allocation and traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

## Explicit inputs and time {#explicit-inputs-and-time}

Every shot delivery export receives or declares all variable inputs, works in seconds, and produces the same composition for the same inputs. It delegates model building and motion evaluation to their owning sources rather than duplicating them.

Review question: can the shot be rendered at an arbitrary declared time without relying on hidden state or frame order?

Sources: [Web Animations timing model](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#timing-model); [glTF 2.0 scene graph concepts](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#scenes)

## Acceptance travels with delivery {#acceptance-travels-with-delivery}

The shot-source population pairs every delivery with observable acceptance conditions, falsifying thresholds, review instants, and view context beside the delivery it judges. Passing is not inferred from a successful render call.

Review question: which reproducible observation would fail this shot even when rendering completes without error?

Sources: [NASA systems engineering handbook on verification](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/); [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

# Instance source obligations

These obligations divide the realization of reviewed population rules as reproducible members across the selected instance-source population without redefining their prototypes.

## Design-owned population {#instance-source-design-ownership}

Every exported owner realizes one reviewed instance document and introduces no unreviewed prototype, member, placement, variation, or tier.

Review question: can every emitted population fact be traced to exactly one reviewed H2?

Sources: [NASA on bidirectional requirement traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

## Stable generated membership {#instance-source-stable-membership}

The same explicit membership, seed, inputs, and prototype identities produce the same ordered ids, transforms, overrides, and representation tiers.

Review question: do equal inputs emit byte-identical membership, ordering, identities, and transforms?

Sources: [OpenUSD on authored point-instancer ids and prototype indices](https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_geom_point_instancer.html)

## Invalid placement is refused {#instance-source-invalid-placement}

Missing prototypes, duplicate ids, non-finite transforms, forbidden overlap, lost contact, and unsupported density or tier requests remain explicit diagnostics.

Review question: does each invalid member fail by stable id before partial population output can pass?

Sources: [OpenUSD on prototype/instance restrictions and unstable generated prototype paths](https://openusd.org/release/api/_usd__page__scenegraph_instancing.html); [NASA on requirement-specific verification results](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

# Instance obligations

These roles are distributed across the instance-design H2 population. Instances own repeated membership and placement; the prototype model remains owned by its model design.

## Addressable instance decisions {#addressable-instance-decisions}

The instance population gives every independently generated set, subgroup, override family, placement rule, or population observation one stable H2.

Review question: which set can change independently but is still bundled under another population owner?

Sources: [NASA on unique, bidirectionally traceable requirements](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

## Prototype and membership {#instance-prototype-membership}

The population identifies each prototype, the exact members of every set, and the rule by which a member enters, leaves, or changes role.

Review question: can every rendered member be traced to one prototype and one declared set membership?

Sources: [OpenUSD on instances associated with shared prototypes](https://openusd.org/release/api/_usd__page__scenegraph_instancing.html)

## Stable identity and transform {#instance-identity-transform}

The population assigns stable instance identities and deterministic position, orientation, scale, parent frame, seed, and ordering rules.

Review question: can the same inputs reproduce the same member at the same transform without relying on traversal or creation order?

Sources: [OpenUSD on point-instancer ids, prototype indices, and transforms](https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_geom_point_instancer.html)

## Variation and representation tiers {#instance-variation-tiers}

The population bounds allowed per-member variation, hero overrides, density, level-of-detail tiers, and transitions without silently creating new models.

Review question: which visible difference is a permitted instance variation, and which requires a separately authored prototype?

Sources: [OpenUSD on shared prototype restrictions and per-instance overrides](https://openusd.org/release/api/_usd__page__scenegraph_instancing.html)

## Placement validity and review {#instance-placement-review}

The population defines overlap, clearance, terrain/host contact, culling, selection, and representative review samples, including worst-case members.

Review question: which deterministic probe exposes collision, drift, unstable membership, or an invalid tier transition?

Sources: [NASA on requirement-specific verification methods and evidence](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

# Map source obligations

These obligations divide the work of turning reviewed world designs into stable engine-facing records across the selected map-source population without making source a second world author.

## Design-owned world construction {#map-source-design-ownership}

Every exported owner realizes one reviewed map document and introduces no unreviewed extent, coordinate interpretation, feature, network, site interface, phase, population, source adoption, or level-of-detail rule.

Review question: can every emitted world fact and derivation be traced to exactly one reviewed map H2?

Sources: [NASA on bidirectional requirement traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/); [OGC CityGML 3.0 on explicit semantic and spatial object structure](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-006r2/21-006r2.html)

## Deterministic resolved world {#map-source-deterministic-world}

Equal reviewed inputs emit identical feature identities, coordinate transforms, topology, states, populations, partitions, and derived quantities regardless of traversal, tile-load, or evaluation order.

Review question: do repeated and differently ordered builds preserve the same identities, bounds, relations, routes, quantities, and states?

Sources: [OGC Topic 2 on coordinate operations](https://docs.ogc.org/as/18-005r5/18-005r5.html); [ECMAScript language specification](https://tc39.es/ecma262/)

## Preserved source lineage {#map-source-preserved-lineage}

Every adopted or authored input keeps its identity, coverage, reference system, accuracy or uncertainty, transformation, conversion loss, and contribution to the resolved features it produced. A derived world view or quantity does not erase the distinction between source fact, authored override, and computed result.

Review question: can every emitted world fact be followed back through the exact current inputs and transformations that authorize it?

Sources: [W3C PROV-O on derivation](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/); [W3C Data Quality Vocabulary on quality measurements and provenance](https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dqv/)

## Invalid or incomplete worlds are refused {#map-source-invalid-world}

Missing source coverage, unresolved coordinate or datum conversion, gaps and overlaps, disconnected required networks, invalid crossings, broken terrain or water contact, incompatible site interfaces, contradictory phases, and incomplete required partitions produce exact diagnostics or bounded unavailable results rather than guessed, closed, or silently substituted world data.

Review question: does each invalid or incomplete map case fail or degrade with the exact feature, relation, source, extent, and affected output named?

Sources: [OGC CityGML 3.0 conformance classes](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-006r2/21-006r2.html#toc45); [NASA on verification results and requirement identity](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

# Map obligations

These roles are distributed across the map-design H2 population. Map owns the broad world's content, coordinates, networks, and state; spaces consumes the adopted site boundary and access interface and owns the site and building topology within it.

## Addressable map decisions {#addressable-map-decisions}

The map population gives every independently citable extent, coordinate basis, feature family, network, phase, source adoption, site interface, derived representation, and world observation one stable H2 owner.

Review question: which world decision could change independently and is still hidden inside another owner's prose, drawing, dataset, or implementation?

This item owns the map population's complete H2 decomposition. The addressable-world principle makes each resulting H2 preserve the identities it states or consumes.

Sources: [NASA on unique, bidirectionally traceable requirements](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/); [OGC CityGML 3.0 on modular thematic ownership](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-006r2/21-006r2.html)

## World extent and site interface {#map-world-site-interface}

The population establishes the canonical world frame, units, declared extent, map feature identities, and every site boundary and access node consumed by a space branch. Map owns the parcel or site boundary as a world feature and the external terrain, water, and transport network through the named access node. Spaces owns the topology, envelope, openings, dimensions, and routes inside that boundary. Settlement-scale building footprints may locate buildings in the world, but the building envelope and interior remain space owners.

Review question: can a site, building, subject, camera, vehicle, or system enter the world at one cited frame and interface without map and spaces authoring the same boundary, route, or building fact twice?

Sources: [OGC Topic 2 on coordinate reference systems and transformations](https://docs.ogc.org/as/18-005r5/18-005r5.html); [buildingSMART on explicit space-boundary relationships](https://standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4_3/HTML/lexical/IfcRelSpaceBoundary.htm)

## Selected world content and relations {#map-world-content-relations}

Across its H2 owners, the population accounts for every world family this production actually uses: terrain and ground, inland or coastal water, vegetation and ecology, parcels and land use, settlements and public space, roads and other transport, crossings and infrastructure, weather and seasonal conditions, temporal change, and externally adopted spatial data or placed assets. Each selected family states its contacts, dependencies, source and confidence, current state, and consequences for other selected families. An unused family is not invented merely to fill a catalogue.

Review question: which selected world feature has no owner for its relation to the terrain, networks, site, population, time state, or source from which its behavior and placement follow?

Sources: [OGC CityGML 3.0 on terrain, water, vegetation, transportation, land use, city objects, and versioning in one model](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-006r2/21-006r2.html); [NASA systems engineering handbook on interfaces and allocated responsibility](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

## World temporal state and alternatives {#map-world-temporal-state}

The population defines the canonical current phase or interval, state transitions the delivery actually uses, and the selection and comparison rule for alternatives. A static work states its fixed state once; it does not manufacture change, while a time-varying work traces every selected feature and network consequence across the affected interval.

Review question: which feature, relation, route, or observation could change with time or alternative selection without the population identifying its valid state and affected outputs?

Sources: [OGC CityGML 3.0 on versions and version transitions](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-006r2/21-006r2.html); [Web Animations on explicit time values and sampled state](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/)

## World scale, partition, and population {#map-world-scale-partition}

The population defines the scale and level-of-detail policy, partition or tile boundaries, deterministic population basis, and identity-preservation rule applicable to the selected map content. An untiled or uninstanced work states that fixed boundary once; it does not manufacture streaming or population work.

Review question: which feature, boundary, route, quantity, or identity could change across scale, detail, tile order, seam, or population evaluation without an explicit preservation or refusal rule?

Sources: [OGC 3D Tiles on hierarchical spatial content and levels of detail](https://www.ogc.org/standard/3dtiles/); [OpenUSD PointInstancer on stable ids, prototype indices, transforms, and extents](https://openusd.org/release/api/class_usd_geom_point_instancer.html)

## World source resolution and staleness {#map-world-source-resolution}

The population defines how adopted and authored inputs become the resolved world, which source identity, coverage, accuracy, uncertainty, transform, and conversion loss survive that derivation, and which dependent maps, routes, quantities, renders, and deliveries become stale when an input or rule changes.

Review question: which resolved world fact cannot be traced to its current input and derivation, or which changed input leaves a dependent result looking current?

Sources: [W3C PROV-O on derivation and invalidation](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/); [W3C Data Quality Vocabulary on quality measurements and provenance](https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dqv/)

## Map review set {#map-review-set}

The population defines a finite set of plan or map views, sections, elevations or profiles, neutral perspectives, traversals, network and quantity checks, state comparisons, source-resolution comparisons, and boundary or seam observations sufficient to falsify every selected world family and its site interfaces independently of dramatic shot composition.

Review question: which finite observations expose every critical terrain, water, feature, route, population, phase, coordinate, and site-contact claim at the scale where it is promised?

Sources: [NASA on definitive requirement verification matrices](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/); [OGC CityGML 3.0 Abstract Test Suite](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-006r2/21-006r2.html#toc45)

# Material source obligations

These obligations divide the work of turning reviewed construction and appearance into deterministic renderer-facing records across the selected material-source population without inventing a finish.

## Design-owned material construction {#material-source-design-ownership}

Every exported owner realizes one reviewed material document and introduces no unreviewed finish, layer, surface assignment, scale, or response.

Review question: can every emitted material fact be traced to exactly one reviewed H2?

Sources: [NASA on bidirectional requirement traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

## Explicit renderer mapping {#material-source-renderer-mapping}

Construction and appearance parameters map explicitly into deterministic renderer values, color spaces, texture transforms, face bindings, and resource identities.

Review question: can each authored parameter be located in the renderer record without inference or a second default?

Sources: [glTF on declarative PBR materials and texture-coordinate interpretation](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#materials)

## Invalid material state is refused {#material-source-invalid-state}

Missing surfaces or textures, invalid ranges, incompatible channels, unsupported states, and budget violations remain named diagnostics rather than silent defaults or substitutions.

Review question: does each invalid material input fail before a renderer can substitute a plausible image?

Sources: [glTF on required indices, media-type agreement, and bounded material fields](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html)

# Material obligations

These roles are distributed across the material-design H2 population. Materials own surface construction and response; models and spaces own the surfaces to which those materials bind.

## Addressable material decisions {#addressable-material-decisions}

The material population gives every independently assignable construction, finish, texture family, junction, state, or material observation one stable H2.

Review question: which material decision could be replaced or reviewed alone and therefore lacks its own owner?

Sources: [NASA on unique, bidirectionally traceable requirements](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

## Material identity and assembly {#material-identity-assembly}

The population names every required construction or finish, its layers or composition, units, thickness or scale where relevant, and the authored substitutions allowed by the delivery.

Review question: which visible or physical material result still depends on an unnamed layer, unit, or substitution?

Sources: [glTF on explicit declarative material parameters](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#materials); [NASA on unique verifiable requirements](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

## Surface assignment {#material-surface-assignment}

The population maps materials to stable model or space surface owners and defines junction, edge, orientation, repetition, and face-specific behavior without taking ownership of the host geometry.

Review question: which face or junction can receive two incompatible finishes or no finish at all?

Sources: [glTF on mesh primitives binding geometry and materials](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#meshes)

## Optical and physical response {#material-response}

The population allocates color space, texture scale, opacity, roughness, metalness, transmission, emission, normal/displacement scale, and any physical behavior actually required by the prototype.

Review question: which observable response is currently an adjective rather than a bounded parameter or reference?

Sources: [glTF on metallic-roughness parameters, opacity, and texture channels](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#materials)

## Material review set {#material-review-set}

The population defines neutral lighting, distance, angle, scale comparison, and state samples that reveal tiling, seams, face errors, and unsupported fidelity.

# Model source obligations

These obligations divide responsibility across the TypeScript population that constructs subjects, objects, environments, and formations from reviewed model documents. Construction owners, deterministic builders, and input boundaries cite the roles they perform; each file supplies a concrete exported class, while the separate exact design edge keeps every exported model type tied to one model document.

## Design-owned construction {#design-owned-construction}

Across the model-source population, exported construction owners realize cited model units and introduce no independent silhouette, dimension, material-zone, hierarchy, or fidelity decision. If implementation exposes a missing design choice, the model document changes first.

Review question: which design unit owns every visible constant and structural choice in this symbol?

Sources: [NASA systems engineering handbook on bidirectional traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/); [glTF 2.0 scene, node, geometry, and material structures](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#concepts)

## Deterministic build {#deterministic-build}

Every model-building entry point maps explicit inputs to the same hierarchy, transforms, geometry, materials, and bounds without hidden randomness, mutable global state, or camera-dependent geometry. Derived values have one owning derivation.

Review question: can two builds with equal inputs be proven structurally and numerically equivalent?

Sources: [ECMAScript specification on execution and numeric values](https://tc39.es/ecma262/); [glTF 2.0 asset and scene graph data model](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#concepts)

## Unsupported fidelity is explicit {#unsupported-fidelity-is-explicit}

Every model-source boundary that accepts a fidelity or articulation request rejects or visibly reports values outside its reviewed design instead of silently substituting a weaker representation. Sources with no such input keep their fixed proxy ceiling explicit. A declared blocking proxy remains acceptable within its stated review purpose.

Review question: what unsupported request would otherwise look deceptively successful, and how is it made explicit?

Sources: [glTF 2.0 extensions and required capability signaling](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#specifying-extensions); [OpenUSD glossary on model kinds and asset organization](https://openusd.org/release/glossary.html)

# Model obligations

These roles must be covered across the model-design H2 population. They are shared representation policies whose distinct contributions may be divided among model H2 owners, not per-unit checklists that every H2 repeats.

## Addressable model decisions {#addressable-model-decisions}

The model population gives every independently implementable, citable, revisable, or reviewable representation decision one stable H2. Geometry allocation, hierarchy, articulation interface, surface partition, fidelity boundary, and review observation with different consumers or change paths are not hidden inside one umbrella unit or repeated in another file. Material construction and response belong in materials; this layer owns only the stable surface that receives one.

Review question: which model decision could change or be implemented independently and therefore still lacks its own H2 owner?

This obligation owns the model-document address structure. The common substantive-completion principle owns the completeness of each addressed design unit, and the exact source edge owns its implementation.

Sources: [NASA on unique identification and one requirement per statement](https://swehb.nasa.gov/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=146540037); [OpenUSD model and asset terminology](https://openusd.org/release/glossary.html)

## Representation ceiling {#representation-ceiling}

The model designs state the production-wide fidelity ceiling and the visible claims that blocking geometry is and is not authorized to make.

Review question: what visual inference must a reviewer refuse to draw from these models?

Sources: [OpenUSD model and asset terminology](https://openusd.org/release/glossary.html)

## Reference scale {#reference-scale}

The model designs nominate the shared scale reference and the rule for deriving or checking the extents of all other represented subjects.

Review question: which represented dimension would reveal a scale mismatch across independently built models?

Sources: [glTF 2.0 coordinate system and units](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#coordinate-system-and-units)

## Articulation ownership {#articulation-ownership}

The model designs state which pivots, bones, morphs, or transform nodes are stable interfaces for motion and which visual parts are deliberately rigid.

Review question: what named model interface may motion change without reconstructing geometry?

Sources: [glTF 2.0 skins and joint hierarchy](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#skins); [glTF 2.0 morph targets](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#morph-targets)

## Model review set {#model-review-set}

The model designs define a finite set of neutral views, backgrounds, and scale comparisons used to judge model construction independently of dramatic shot composition.

Review question: which repeated views make regressions comparable across model revisions?

Sources: [Academy Digital Source Master project](https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/academy-digital-source-master)

## Representation completion account {#model-representation-completion}

The complete model population accounts for every promised representation layer, shared scale relation, hierarchy boundary, stable surface or articulation interface, declared limitation, and observable acceptance owner. It reports separately whether the representation is structurally valid and whether it is semantically complete for its consumers; neither verdict implies the other.

Review question: which model passes structural validation while still leaving a promised layer, scale relation, interface, limitation, or observation without an owner?

Sources: [glTF 2.0 nodes, meshes, skins, and units](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html); [NASA systems engineering handbook on verification-ready requirements](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

# Motion source obligations

These obligations divide responsibility across reusable TypeScript motion constants and constructors. Constants carry reviewed values, while callable constructors own time mapping and input refusal; the separate exact design edge keeps every exported function and property tied to one motion document.

## Design-owned transition {#design-owned-transition}

# Motion obligations

These roles must be covered across the motion-design H2 population. They define shared transition policy whose distinct contributions may be divided among motion H2 owners, rather than forcing every H2 to repeat every role.

## Addressable motion decisions {#addressable-motion-decisions}

The motion population gives every independently callable, composable, revisable, or reviewable transition or observation one stable H2. A transition with its own entry, exit, time domain, parameter set, interruption behavior, or consumer does not hide under another motion's heading, and a review protocol that several transitions share belongs to the population obligation rather than being copied.

Review question: which timed behavior could be selected, changed, or falsified independently and therefore still lacks its own H2 owner?

This obligation owns motion-document address structure. The common substantive-completion principle owns each unit's completeness, and the exact source edge owns its implementation.

Sources: [NASA on unique identification and one requirement per statement](https://swehb.nasa.gov/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=146540037); [Web Animations timing model](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#timing-model)

## Time base {#time-base}

The motion designs consume the settings time unit and define the production-wide mapping, clamping, and sampling convention used by normalized progress functions.

Review question: how does any render time map to one deterministic motion phase?

Sources: [Web Animations time values and timing model](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#timing-model)

## Contact policy {#contact-policy}

The motion designs establish how contact targets, penetration, separation, and tolerance are measured for motions that touch or remain planted on another reviewed design target.

Review question: which numeric condition distinguishes maintained contact from visible drift or penetration?

Sources: [NIST Technical Note 1297](https://www.nist.gov/pml/nist-technical-note-1297)

## Composition and interruption {#composition-interruption}

The motion designs state whether concurrent motions may compose, which property wins on conflict, and what state is used when a motion is interrupted or followed by another.

Review question: what exact state crosses a boundary between two motions that address the same model property?

Sources: [Web Animations composite operations](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#effect-composition)

## Motion review set {#motion-review-set}

The motion designs define the instants, spatial views, state samples, and tolerances used to review paths and contacts independently of screenplay interpretation.

Review question: which finite observations falsify the transition rather than merely show that it ran?

Sources: [Web Animations timing model](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#timing-model); [NASA systems engineering handbook on verification](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/systems-engineering-handbook/)

# Space source obligations

These obligations divide the work of turning reviewed topology into stable engine-facing records across the selected space-source population without making source a second spatial author.

## Design-owned topology {#space-source-design-ownership}

Every exported owner realizes one reviewed space document and introduces no unreviewed place, boundary, opening, route, dimension, or access rule.

Review question: can every emitted spatial fact be traced to exactly one reviewed H2?

Sources: [NASA on bidirectional requirement traceability](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)

## Stable spatial identities {#space-source-stable-identities}

Every emitted space, surface, opening, level, zone, and route keeps stable ids, frames, units, bounds, and parent relationships across repeated builds.

Review question: do equal inputs emit identical identities, frames, topology, and dimensions?

Sources: [glTF on coordinate units and node hierarchy](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#coordinate-system-and-units); [buildingSMART on explicit space-boundary relations](https://standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4_3/HTML/lexical/IfcRelSpaceBoundary.htm)

## Invalid topology is refused {#space-source-invalid-topology}

Cycles, missing hosts, contradictory bounds, blocked required routes, and exterior/interior mismatches produce explicit diagnostics rather than repaired or guessed geometry.

Review question: does each invalid topology case fail with its exact owner and cause?

Sources: [glTF on node hierarchy as disjoint strict trees](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html#nodes-and-hierarchy); [NASA on verification results and requirement identity](https://www.nasa.gov/reference/system-engineering-handbook-appendix/)
